Compute the largest positive integer \( n \) such that

\[
n \text{ divides } (\lfloor \sqrt{n} \rfloor)!^{n!} + 450.
\]

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let  
\[
a=\lfloor \sqrt n\rfloor,\qquad B=(a!)^{n!}.
\]
Assume \(n\mid B+450\).

For any prime \(p\mid n\):

- If \(p\le a\), then \(p\mid a!\), so \(p\mid B\). Hence \(p\mid B+450\implies p\mid 450\). Thus \(p\in\{2,3,5\}\).
- If \(p>a\), then \(\gcd(a!,p)=1\). Also \(p-1<n\), so \(p-1\mid n!\). By Fermat,
  \[
  B\equiv 1\pmod p,
  \]
  so \(p\mid B+450\implies p\mid 451\). Thus \(p\in\{11,41\}\).

Therefore all prime divisors of \(n\) lie in \(\{2,3,5,11,41\}\), with restrictions:
\[
v_2(n)\le1,\quad v_3(n)\le2,\quad v_5(n)\le2,\quad v_{11}(n)\le1,\quad v_{41}(n)\le1.
\]

If \(a\ge 41\), then \(11,41\) cannot divide \(n\), so \(n\mid 2\cdot 3^2\cdot5^2=450\), impossible since \(n\ge a^2\ge1681\). Hence \(a\le40\).

If \(11\le a\le40\), then \(11\nmid n\), so
\[
n\mid 2\cdot3^2\cdot5^2\cdot41=18450.
\]

Now suppose \(n>1230\). Then \(a\ge35\), so \(35\le a\le40\) and \(n<41^2=1681\). But the divisors of \(18450\) jump from
\[
1230=41\cdot30
\]
to
\[
1845=41\cdot45>1680,
\]
so no divisor of \(18450\) lies in \((1230,1680]\). Thus no valid \(n\) exceeds \(1230\).

Finally, check \(n=1230\). Here \(a=35\), and
\[
1230=2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot41.
\]
Modulo \(2,3,5\), both \(35!\) and \(450\) are divisible by the prime. Modulo \(41\), since \(40\mid1230!\),
\[
(35!)^{1230!}\equiv1\pmod{41},
\]
and
\[
1+450=451\equiv0\pmod{41}.
\]
Thus \(1230\mid (35!)^{1230!}+450\).

\[
\boxed{1230}
\]
